knowledge_point.title: Finding the Jacobian of a Three-Dimensional Transformation

question.:question/problem:
Find the Jacobian determinant of the transformation $T,$ defined as

$$
T:\begin{bmatrix}u \\ v \\ w\end{bmatrix}⟶\begin{bmatrix}- \ln{\left(u v w \right)} \\ 2 u - 4 w \\ - 4 u v\end{bmatrix}.
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
For a transformation 

$$
T:\begin{bmatrix}u \\ v \\ w\end{bmatrix}\to \begin{bmatrix}x(u,v,w) \\ y(u,v,w) \\ z(u,v,w)\end{bmatrix},
$$

the Jacobian determinant of $T,$ denoted $\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)},$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)} & =\begin{vmatrix}\frac{∂x}{∂u} & \frac{∂x}{∂v} & \frac{∂x}{∂w} \\ \frac{∂y}{∂u} & \frac{∂y}{∂v} & \frac{∂y}{∂w} \\ \frac{∂z}{∂u} & \frac{∂z}{∂v} & \frac{∂z}{∂w}\end{vmatrix}.\end{aligned}
$$

Here, we have 

$$
x(u,v,w)=- \ln{\left(u v w \right)}\, y(u,v,w)=2 u - 4 w\, z(u,v,w)=- 4 u v.
$$

First, we find the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂x}{∂u} & =- \frac{1}{u} & \frac{∂x}{∂v} & =- \frac{1}{v} & \frac{∂x}{∂w} & =- \frac{1}{w} \\ \frac{∂y}{∂u} & =2 & \frac{∂y}{∂v} & =0 & \frac{∂y}{∂w} & =-4 \\ \frac{∂z}{∂u} & =- 4 v & \frac{∂z}{∂v} & =- 4 u, & \frac{∂z}{∂w} & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the corresponding Jacobian determinant is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)} & =\begin{vmatrix}- \frac{1}{u} & - \frac{1}{v} & - \frac{1}{w} \\ 2 & 0 & -4 \\ - 4 v & - 4 u & 0\end{vmatrix} \\  & =\left(- \frac{1}{w}\right)(-1)^{1+3}\begin{vmatrix}2 & 0 \\ - 4 v & - 4 u\end{vmatrix}+\left(-4\right)(-1)^{2+3}\begin{vmatrix}- \frac{1}{u} & - \frac{1}{v} \\ - 4 v & - 4 u\end{vmatrix} \\  & =\left(- \frac{1}{w}\right)\left(- 8 u-\left(0\right)\right)+\left(4\right)\left(4-\left(4\right)\right) \\  & =\frac{8 u}{w}.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem:
Find the Jacobian determinant of the transformation $T,$ defined as

$$
T:\begin{bmatrix}u \\ v \\ w\end{bmatrix}⟶\begin{bmatrix}- u - v \cos{\left(\theta \right)} - w \sin{\left(\theta \right)} \\ 2 v \\ - 4 u \sin{\left(\theta \right)} - 4 w\end{bmatrix}.
$$

You may assume that $\theta$ is a fixed constant.
question.:question/worked-solution:
For a transformation 

$$
T:\begin{bmatrix}u \\ v \\ w\end{bmatrix}\to \begin{bmatrix}x(u,v,w) \\ y(u,v,w) \\ z(u,v,w)\end{bmatrix},
$$

the Jacobian determinant of $T,$ denoted $\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)},$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)} & =\begin{vmatrix}\frac{∂x}{∂u} & \frac{∂x}{∂v} & \frac{∂x}{∂w} \\ \frac{∂y}{∂u} & \frac{∂y}{∂v} & \frac{∂y}{∂w} \\ \frac{∂z}{∂u} & \frac{∂z}{∂v} & \frac{∂z}{∂w}\end{vmatrix}.\end{aligned}
$$

Here, we have 

$$
x(u,v,w)=- u - v \cos{\left(\theta \right)} - w \sin{\left(\theta \right)}\, y(u,v,w)=2 v\, z(u,v,w)=- 4 u \sin{\left(\theta \right)} - 4 w.
$$

First, we find the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂x}{∂u} & =-1 & \frac{∂x}{∂v} & =- \cos{\left(\theta \right)} & \frac{∂x}{∂w} & =- \sin{\left(\theta \right)} \\ \frac{∂y}{∂u} & =0 & \frac{∂y}{∂v} & =2 & \frac{∂y}{∂w} & =0 \\ \frac{∂z}{∂u} & =- 4 \sin{\left(\theta \right)} & \frac{∂z}{∂v} & =0, & \frac{∂z}{∂w} & =-4\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the corresponding Jacobian determinant is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)} & =\begin{vmatrix}-1 & - \cos{\left(\theta \right)} & - \sin{\left(\theta \right)} \\ 0 & 2 & 0 \\ - 4 \sin{\left(\theta \right)} & 0 & -4\end{vmatrix} \\  & =\left(2\right)(-1)^{2+2}\begin{vmatrix}-1 & - \sin{\left(\theta \right)} \\ - 4 \sin{\left(\theta \right)} & -4\end{vmatrix} \\  & =\left(2\right)\left(4-\left(4 \sin^{2}{\left(\theta \right)}\right)\right) \\  & =8 \cos^{2}{\left(\theta \right)}.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem:
Find the Jacobian determinant of the transformation $T,$ defined as

$$
T:\begin{bmatrix}u \\ v \\ w\end{bmatrix}⟶\begin{bmatrix}- u + 2 \cos{\left(w \right)} \\ - 4 v \\ 3 w - 4 \cos{\left(u \right)}\end{bmatrix}.
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
For a transformation 

$$
T:\begin{bmatrix}u \\ v \\ w\end{bmatrix}\to \begin{bmatrix}x(u,v,w) \\ y(u,v,w) \\ z(u,v,w)\end{bmatrix},
$$

the Jacobian determinant of $T,$ denoted $\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)},$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)} & =\begin{vmatrix}\frac{∂x}{∂u} & \frac{∂x}{∂v} & \frac{∂x}{∂w} \\ \frac{∂y}{∂u} & \frac{∂y}{∂v} & \frac{∂y}{∂w} \\ \frac{∂z}{∂u} & \frac{∂z}{∂v} & \frac{∂z}{∂w}\end{vmatrix}.\end{aligned}
$$

Here, we have 

$$
x(u,v,w)=- u + 2 \cos{\left(w \right)}\, y(u,v,w)=- 4 v\, z(u,v,w)=3 w - 4 \cos{\left(u \right)}.
$$

First, we find the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂x}{∂u} & =-1 & \frac{∂x}{∂v} & =0 & \frac{∂x}{∂w} & =- 2 \sin{\left(w \right)} \\ \frac{∂y}{∂u} & =0 & \frac{∂y}{∂v} & =-4 & \frac{∂y}{∂w} & =0 \\ \frac{∂z}{∂u} & =4 \sin{\left(u \right)} & \frac{∂z}{∂v} & =0, & \frac{∂z}{∂w} & =3\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the corresponding Jacobian determinant is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)} & =\begin{vmatrix}-1 & 0 & - 2 \sin{\left(w \right)} \\ 0 & -4 & 0 \\ 4 \sin{\left(u \right)} & 0 & 3\end{vmatrix} \\  & =\left(-4\right)(-1)^{2+2}\begin{vmatrix}-1 & - 2 \sin{\left(w \right)} \\ 4 \sin{\left(u \right)} & 3\end{vmatrix} \\  & =- 32 \sin{\left(u \right)} \sin{\left(w \right)} + 12.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem:
Find the Jacobian determinant of the transformation $T,$ defined as

$$
T:\begin{bmatrix}u \\ v \\ w\end{bmatrix}⟶\begin{bmatrix}- u e^{w} \\ - 2 u - 4 w \\ 4 v + w e^{u}\end{bmatrix}.
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
For a transformation 

$$
T:\begin{bmatrix}u \\ v \\ w\end{bmatrix}\to \begin{bmatrix}x(u,v,w) \\ y(u,v,w) \\ z(u,v,w)\end{bmatrix},
$$

the Jacobian determinant of $T,$ denoted $\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)},$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)} & =\begin{vmatrix}\frac{∂x}{∂u} & \frac{∂x}{∂v} & \frac{∂x}{∂w} \\ \frac{∂y}{∂u} & \frac{∂y}{∂v} & \frac{∂y}{∂w} \\ \frac{∂z}{∂u} & \frac{∂z}{∂v} & \frac{∂z}{∂w}\end{vmatrix}.\end{aligned}
$$

Here, we have 

$$
x(u,v,w)=- u e^{w}\, y(u,v,w)=- 2 u - 4 w\, z(u,v,w)=4 v + w e^{u}.
$$

First, we find the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂x}{∂u} & =- e^{w} & \frac{∂x}{∂v} & =0 & \frac{∂x}{∂w} & =- u e^{w} \\ \frac{∂y}{∂u} & =-2 & \frac{∂y}{∂v} & =0 & \frac{∂y}{∂w} & =-4 \\ \frac{∂z}{∂u} & =w e^{u} & \frac{∂z}{∂v} & =4, & \frac{∂z}{∂w} & =e^{u}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the corresponding Jacobian determinant is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)} & =\begin{vmatrix}- e^{w} & 0 & - u e^{w} \\ -2 & 0 & -4 \\ w e^{u} & 4 & e^{u}\end{vmatrix} \\  & =\left(4\right)(-1)^{3+2}\begin{vmatrix}- e^{w} & - u e^{w} \\ -2 & -4\end{vmatrix} \\  & =\left(-4\right)\left(4 e^{w}-\left(2 u e^{w}\right)\right) \\  & =8 \left(u - 2\right) e^{w}.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem:
Find the Jacobian determinant of the transformation $T,$ defined as

$$
T:\begin{bmatrix}u \\ v \\ w\end{bmatrix}⟶\begin{bmatrix}- u^{2} + 2 v^{2} \\ - 4 u - 4 w \\ - 3 v\end{bmatrix}.
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
For a transformation 

$$
T:\begin{bmatrix}u \\ v \\ w\end{bmatrix}\to \begin{bmatrix}x(u,v,w) \\ y(u,v,w) \\ z(u,v,w)\end{bmatrix},
$$

the Jacobian determinant of $T,$ denoted $\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)},$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)} & =\begin{vmatrix}\frac{∂x}{∂u} & \frac{∂x}{∂v} & \frac{∂x}{∂w} \\ \frac{∂y}{∂u} & \frac{∂y}{∂v} & \frac{∂y}{∂w} \\ \frac{∂z}{∂u} & \frac{∂z}{∂v} & \frac{∂z}{∂w}\end{vmatrix}.\end{aligned}
$$

Here, we have 

$$
x(u,v,w)=- u^{2} + 2 v^{2}\, y(u,v,w)=- 4 u - 4 w\, z(u,v,w)=- 3 v.
$$

First, we find the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂x}{∂u} & =- 2 u & \frac{∂x}{∂v} & =4 v & \frac{∂x}{∂w} & =0 \\ \frac{∂y}{∂u} & =-4 & \frac{∂y}{∂v} & =0 & \frac{∂y}{∂w} & =-4 \\ \frac{∂z}{∂u} & =0 & \frac{∂z}{∂v} & =-3, & \frac{∂z}{∂w} & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the corresponding Jacobian determinant is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)} & =\begin{vmatrix}- 2 u & 4 v & 0 \\ -4 & 0 & -4 \\ 0 & -3 & 0\end{vmatrix} \\  & =\left(-3\right)(-1)^{3+2}\begin{vmatrix}- 2 u & 0 \\ -4 & -4\end{vmatrix} \\  & =\left(3\right)\left(8 u-\left(0\right)\right) \\  & =24 u.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem:
Find the Jacobian determinant of the transformation $T,$ defined as

$$
T:\begin{bmatrix}u \\ v \\ w\end{bmatrix}⟶\begin{bmatrix}3 v \\ 2 u^{2} + 3 \cos{\left(v w \right)} \\ 4 v w\end{bmatrix}.
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
For a transformation 

$$
T:\begin{bmatrix}u \\ v \\ w\end{bmatrix}\to \begin{bmatrix}x(u,v,w) \\ y(u,v,w) \\ z(u,v,w)\end{bmatrix},
$$

the Jacobian determinant of $T,$ denoted $\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)},$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)} & =\begin{vmatrix}\frac{∂x}{∂u} & \frac{∂x}{∂v} & \frac{∂x}{∂w} \\ \frac{∂y}{∂u} & \frac{∂y}{∂v} & \frac{∂y}{∂w} \\ \frac{∂z}{∂u} & \frac{∂z}{∂v} & \frac{∂z}{∂w}\end{vmatrix}.\end{aligned}
$$

Here, we have 

$$
x(u,v,w)=3 v\, y(u,v,w)=2 u^{2} + 3 \cos{\left(v w \right)}\, z(u,v,w)=4 v w.
$$

First, we find the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂x}{∂u} & =0 & \frac{∂x}{∂v} & =3 & \frac{∂x}{∂w} & =0 \\ \frac{∂y}{∂u} & =4 u & \frac{∂y}{∂v} & =- 3 w \sin{\left(v w \right)} & \frac{∂y}{∂w} & =- 3 v \sin{\left(v w \right)} \\ \frac{∂z}{∂u} & =0 & \frac{∂z}{∂v} & =4 w, & \frac{∂z}{∂w} & =4 v\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the corresponding Jacobian determinant is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)} & =\begin{vmatrix}0 & 3 & 0 \\ 4 u & - 3 w \sin{\left(v w \right)} & - 3 v \sin{\left(v w \right)} \\ 0 & 4 w & 4 v\end{vmatrix} \\  & =\left(3\right)(-1)^{1+2}\begin{vmatrix}4 u & - 3 v \sin{\left(v w \right)} \\ 0 & 4 v\end{vmatrix} \\  & =\left(-3\right)\left(16 u v-\left(0\right)\right) \\  & =- 48 u v.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem:
Find the Jacobian determinant of the transformation $T$ that maps the $uvw$-space into the $xyz$-space by means of the equations

$$
x=- u \sin{\left(v \right)} \cos{\left(w \right)}\, y=2 u \sin{\left(v \right)} \sin{\left(w \right)}\, z=- 4 u \cos{\left(v \right)}.
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
For a transformation 

$$
T:\begin{bmatrix}u \\ v \\ w\end{bmatrix}\to \begin{bmatrix}x(u,v,w) \\ y(u,v,w) \\ z(u,v,w)\end{bmatrix},
$$

the Jacobian determinant of $T,$ denoted $\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)},$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)} & =\begin{vmatrix}\frac{∂x}{∂u} & \frac{∂x}{∂v} & \frac{∂x}{∂w} \\ \frac{∂y}{∂u} & \frac{∂y}{∂v} & \frac{∂y}{∂w} \\ \frac{∂z}{∂u} & \frac{∂z}{∂v} & \frac{∂z}{∂w}\end{vmatrix}.\end{aligned}
$$

First, we find the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂x}{∂u} & =- \sin{\left(v \right)} \cos{\left(w \right)} & \frac{∂x}{∂v} & =- u \cos{\left(v \right)} \cos{\left(w \right)} & \frac{∂x}{∂w} & =u \sin{\left(v \right)} \sin{\left(w \right)} \\ \frac{∂y}{∂u} & =2 \sin{\left(v \right)} \sin{\left(w \right)} & \frac{∂y}{∂v} & =2 u \sin{\left(w \right)} \cos{\left(v \right)} & \frac{∂y}{∂w} & =2 u \sin{\left(v \right)} \cos{\left(w \right)} \\ \frac{∂z}{∂u} & =- 4 \cos{\left(v \right)} & \frac{∂z}{∂v} & =4 u \sin{\left(v \right)} & \frac{∂z}{∂w} & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the corresponding Jacobian determinant is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)} & =\begin{vmatrix}- \sin{\left(v \right)} \cos{\left(w \right)} & - u \cos{\left(v \right)} \cos{\left(w \right)} & u \sin{\left(v \right)} \sin{\left(w \right)} \\ 2 \sin{\left(v \right)} \sin{\left(w \right)} & 2 u \sin{\left(w \right)} \cos{\left(v \right)} & 2 u \sin{\left(v \right)} \cos{\left(w \right)} \\ - 4 \cos{\left(v \right)} & 4 u \sin{\left(v \right)} & 0\end{vmatrix} \\  & =\left(- 4 \cos{\left(v \right)}\right)(-1)^{3+1}\begin{vmatrix}- u \cos{\left(v \right)} \cos{\left(w \right)} & u \sin{\left(v \right)} \sin{\left(w \right)} \\ 2 u \sin{\left(w \right)} \cos{\left(v \right)} & 2 u \sin{\left(v \right)} \cos{\left(w \right)}\end{vmatrix}+\left(4 u \sin{\left(v \right)}\right)(-1)^{3+2}\begin{vmatrix}- \sin{\left(v \right)} \cos{\left(w \right)} & u \sin{\left(v \right)} \sin{\left(w \right)} \\ 2 \sin{\left(v \right)} \sin{\left(w \right)} & 2 u \sin{\left(v \right)} \cos{\left(w \right)}\end{vmatrix} \\  & =\left(8 u^{2} \sin{\left(v \right)} \cos^{2}{\left(v \right)}\right)\left(\cos^2 w+\sin^2 w\right)+\left(8 u^{2} \sin^{3}{\left(v \right)}\right)\left(\cos^2 w+\sin^2 w\right) \\  & =\left(8 u^{2} \sin{\left(v \right)} \cos^{2}{\left(v \right)}\right)+\left(8 u^{2} \sin^{3}{\left(v \right)}\right) \\  & =8 u^{2} \sin{\left(v \right)}\left(\cos^2 v+\sin^2 v\right) \\  & =8 u^{2} \sin{\left(v \right)}.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem:
Find the Jacobian determinant of the transformation $T$ that maps the $uvw$-space into the $xyz$-space by means of the equations

$$
x=- v + 2 w\, y=- 4 u - 4 w\, z=3 u + 2 v.
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
For a transformation 

$$
T:\begin{bmatrix}u \\ v \\ w\end{bmatrix}\to \begin{bmatrix}x(u,v,w) \\ y(u,v,w) \\ z(u,v,w)\end{bmatrix},
$$

the Jacobian determinant of $T,$ denoted $\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)},$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)} & =\begin{vmatrix}\frac{∂x}{∂u} & \frac{∂x}{∂v} & \frac{∂x}{∂w} \\ \frac{∂y}{∂u} & \frac{∂y}{∂v} & \frac{∂y}{∂w} \\ \frac{∂z}{∂u} & \frac{∂z}{∂v} & \frac{∂z}{∂w}\end{vmatrix}.\end{aligned}
$$

First, we find the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂x}{∂u} & =0 & \frac{∂x}{∂v} & =-1 & \frac{∂x}{∂w} & =2 \\ \frac{∂y}{∂u} & =-4 & \frac{∂y}{∂v} & =0 & \frac{∂y}{∂w} & =-4 \\ \frac{∂z}{∂u} & =3 & \frac{∂z}{∂v} & =2 & \frac{∂z}{∂w} & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the corresponding Jacobian determinant is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)} & =\begin{vmatrix}0 & -1 & 2 \\ -4 & 0 & -4 \\ 3 & 2 & 0\end{vmatrix} \\  & =\left(-1\right)(-1)^{1+2}\begin{vmatrix}-4 & -4 \\ 3 & 0\end{vmatrix}+\left(2\right)(-1)^{1+3}\begin{vmatrix}-4 & 0 \\ 3 & 2\end{vmatrix} \\  & =\left(0-\left(-12\right)\right)+\left(2\right)\left(-8-\left(0\right)\right) \\  & =-4.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem:
Find the Jacobian determinant of the transformation $T$ that maps the $uvw$-space into the $xyz$-space by means of the equations

$$
x=- u v^{2} + 2 w\, y=- 4 u^{3} - 4 v\, z=3 u v.
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
For a transformation 

$$
T:\begin{bmatrix}u \\ v \\ w\end{bmatrix}\to \begin{bmatrix}x(u,v,w) \\ y(u,v,w) \\ z(u,v,w)\end{bmatrix},
$$

the Jacobian determinant of $T,$ denoted $\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)},$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)} & =\begin{vmatrix}\frac{∂x}{∂u} & \frac{∂x}{∂v} & \frac{∂x}{∂w} \\ \frac{∂y}{∂u} & \frac{∂y}{∂v} & \frac{∂y}{∂w} \\ \frac{∂z}{∂u} & \frac{∂z}{∂v} & \frac{∂z}{∂w}\end{vmatrix}.\end{aligned}
$$

First, we find the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂x}{∂u} & =- v^{2} & \frac{∂x}{∂v} & =- 2 u v & \frac{∂x}{∂w} & =2 \\ \frac{∂y}{∂u} & =- 12 u^{2} & \frac{∂y}{∂v} & =-4 & \frac{∂y}{∂w} & =0 \\ \frac{∂z}{∂u} & =3 v & \frac{∂z}{∂v} & =3 u & \frac{∂z}{∂w} & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the corresponding Jacobian determinant is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)} & =\begin{vmatrix}- v^{2} & - 2 u v & 2 \\ - 12 u^{2} & -4 & 0 \\ 3 v & 3 u & 0\end{vmatrix} \\  & =\left(2\right)(-1)^{1+3}\begin{vmatrix}- 12 u^{2} & -4 \\ 3 v & 3 u\end{vmatrix} \\  & =- 72 u^{3} + 24 v.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem:
Find the Jacobian determinant of the transformation $T$ that maps the $uvw$-space into the $xyz$-space by means of the equations

$$
x=- u \cos{\left(\theta \right)} - v \sin{\left(\theta \right)}\, y=- 2 u \sin{\left(\theta \right)} + 2 v \cos{\left(\theta \right)}\, z=- 4 w.
$$

You may assume that $\theta$ is a fixed constant.
question.:question/worked-solution:
For a transformation 

$$
T:\begin{bmatrix}u \\ v \\ w\end{bmatrix}\to \begin{bmatrix}x(u,v,w) \\ y(u,v,w) \\ z(u,v,w)\end{bmatrix},
$$

the Jacobian determinant of $T,$ denoted $\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)},$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)} & =\begin{vmatrix}\frac{∂x}{∂u} & \frac{∂x}{∂v} & \frac{∂x}{∂w} \\ \frac{∂y}{∂u} & \frac{∂y}{∂v} & \frac{∂y}{∂w} \\ \frac{∂z}{∂u} & \frac{∂z}{∂v} & \frac{∂z}{∂w}\end{vmatrix}.\end{aligned}
$$

First, we find the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂x}{∂u} & =- \cos{\left(\theta \right)} & \frac{∂x}{∂v} & =- \sin{\left(\theta \right)} & \frac{∂x}{∂w} & =0 \\ \frac{∂y}{∂u} & =- 2 \sin{\left(\theta \right)} & \frac{∂y}{∂v} & =2 \cos{\left(\theta \right)} & \frac{∂y}{∂w} & =0 \\ \frac{∂z}{∂u} & =0 & \frac{∂z}{∂v} & =0 & \frac{∂z}{∂w} & =-4\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the corresponding Jacobian determinant is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)} & =\begin{vmatrix}- \cos{\left(\theta \right)} & - \sin{\left(\theta \right)} & 0 \\ - 2 \sin{\left(\theta \right)} & 2 \cos{\left(\theta \right)} & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & -4\end{vmatrix} \\  & =\left(-4\right)(-1)^{3+3}\begin{vmatrix}- \cos{\left(\theta \right)} & - \sin{\left(\theta \right)} \\ - 2 \sin{\left(\theta \right)} & 2 \cos{\left(\theta \right)}\end{vmatrix} \\  & =\left(8 \cos^{2}{\left(\theta \right)}\right)+\left(8 \sin^{2}{\left(\theta \right)}\right) \\  & =8.\end{aligned}
$$

$$

First, we find the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂x}{∂u} & =- a & \frac{∂x}{∂v} & =0 & \frac{∂x}{∂w} & =0 \\ \frac{∂y}{∂u} & =0 & \frac{∂y}{∂v} & =2 b & \frac{∂y}{∂w} & =0 \\ \frac{∂z}{∂u} & =0 & \frac{∂z}{∂v} & =0 & \frac{∂z}{∂w} & =- 4 c\end{aligned}

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)} & =\begin{vmatrix}- a & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 b & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & - 4 c\end{vmatrix} \\  & =\left(- a\right)(-1)^{1+1}\begin{vmatrix}2 b & 0 \\ 0 & - 4 c\end{vmatrix} \\  & =\left(- a\right)\left(- 8 b c-\left(0\right)\right) \\  & =8 a b c.\end{aligned}
